text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong called on all Singaporeans to make learning a part of their everyday lives and said the country's future would hinge of the people's ability to do this.
- Members of Parliament took Malaysia to task over the strained ties between the two countries and said they found the abuses and threats from across the Causeway unacceptable.
- The value of shares traded on the Singapore bourse last month fell 11.7 percent to Singapore S$6.8 billion year-on-year, the first decline since January.
- The Ang family of the Petaling Garden group says it may consider selling its 14 percent stake in Parkway Holdings to DBS Land if it is offered the right price.

- Singapore's trade with Cambodia, Laos and Burma is expected to grow at least 10 percent a year to Singapore $3.2 billion by 2000 with Rangoon's entry into ASEAN, the Trade Development Board (TDB) says.
- Singapore Telecom will cut its international direct dialling (IDD) rates to 106 "less popular" destinations by up to 15 percent.
- Malaysia and Indonesia are embroiled in a dispute whose outcome could decide which of them will dominate the palm oil industry.
- Less than half of Ekran Bhd's rights issue has been subscribed, a result that could dampen sentiment on the company's flotation of its M$15.5 billion Bakun hydroelectric dam in Sarawak.
- Marco Polo Developments saw net profits rise 12.9 percent to Singapore $18.27 million for the year ended March 1997, higher than expected.
- District Judge Khoo Oon Soo ruled that business broker Peter Tay Huay Hong will face both charges of conspiracy to cheat Amcol Holdings and of receiving money stolen from the company in one trial.
- Jurong Cement saw group after-tax profit fall 2.7 percent to Singapore $21.2 million in the year ended March 31 despite good gains in turnover.
- San Teh Ltd, which makes rubber keypads, has raised its shareholdings in several subsidiary companies.
- Mainboard-listed Clipsal Industries plans to raise US$33.5 million through the placement of nine million new shares to fund its expansion programme and for additional working capital.
- Ralph-Peter Jentes, recruited to run CDL Hotels' worldwide chain, has quit the company less than a year after joining it.
